stem:
Meena stands in her school corridor holding a small plane mirror. She tilts the mirror so that sunlight coming through the window falls on it. A bright patch of light appears on the classroom wall behind her.
Why does the bright patch appear on the wall?

options.text: The mirror makes its own light because it is shiny.
The sunlight passes through the mirror and lights up the wall.
The mirror changes the direction of the sunlight falling on it, so the light is reflected onto the wall.
The wall absorbs sunlight from the window and gives it out as a bright patch.

teacher.key_rationale: A plane mirror is a shiny surface; when sunlight falls on it, the mirror redirects the light by reflection, producing a bright patch on the wall. Mirrors do not generate light (A is wrong), light does not pass through a mirror (B is wrong), and the wall merely receives the reflected light rather than emitting stored light (D is wrong). Hence C.
